transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm glad you're here. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I guess nothing really feels like mine anymore. I used to get excited about things, you know? Checking out murals, going for runs, basketball... even just making a really good drink at work. I'm a bartender. But lately, I just kind of stand there. It's like I don't care about any of it anymore.
How long has it been since you started noticing that you don't care about things the way you used to?

It's been about two months. Yeah, right around two months. That's when the bar got bought out by new owners. Everything I had been working toward there just... got changed around. I guess that's when I started noticing it.
Besides not caring about things, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over these past two months?

Well, my sleep has definitely been off. I'll lie down at night, and I'm really tired, but my head just keeps going. I just lay there going over every mistake I made at work. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up around four or five in the morning. Once I'm up, that's it, I just can't get back down.

Over your lifetime, have you ever had periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was significantly elevated or 'high'?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had good days where things were going well at the bar and I felt decent, but nothing like what you're describing. I've never felt unusually high or like I didn't need to sleep. It's pretty much just been this low feeling lately.
Before these past two months, have you ever had another period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things you normally enjoyed?

No, I haven't. I mean, sure, I've had bad weeks before... just normal stress or feeling down for a couple days. But nothing that lasted two weeks, and never anything where I just completely stopped caring like I have lately. This is really the first time it's been this bad.
Over these past two months, have you been feeling guilty about things, or like you're worthless, or blaming yourself for what happened at work?

Yeah, I have. I just... I keep thinking about how I let down the younger bartenders. And there were these artists I promised space to at the bar, and I feel like I completely wrecked their shot. I just keep blaming myself for it. Honestly, it feels like I deserve whatever happens to me now for messing that up for them.
Have you had any thoughts about death or about harming yourself over these past two months?

No, I haven't. I know I just said I feel like I deserve whatever happens, but... I haven't actually thought about hurting myself or wanting to die. It just hasn't crossed my mind to do anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over these past two months?

Yeah, definitely. I just don't really have an appetite anymore. Most days, I honestly forget to eat entirely until my hands start shaking while I'm working behind the bar. Even then, I usually just wait until after closing and try to grab a few bites of whatever's left over or cold. But lately, even just looking at the food makes me feel kind of sick, so I haven't been eating much at all. I haven't weighed myself, but I know I've dropped some weight.
Over these past two months, have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, making decisions, or remembering things?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's been getting pretty bad at work. Doing inventory used to be totally automatic for me, just second nature. But lately, I'll just stand there staring at the bottles, and I'll lose count like three times in a row. And making decisions... I just freeze up. Even over something really simple, like trying to figure out which garnish I need to restock. I just can't seem to think straight.

During these past two months, have you experienced any beliefs that felt absolutely true to you, even though others might have disagreed? For example, have you believed something about yourself or the world that others told you wasn't actually true, but you were convinced it was?

Yeah, I have. I mean, people keep telling me the owners already had their plan before any of this happened, but... I just can't shake the fact that I poisoned that place somehow. It's like my ideas ruined the bar, and now everybody there is paying for it because of me. Other people say that's not true, but I'm just convinced it's all my fault.

When you think about poisoning the bar with your ideas, can you understand why other people don't see it that way, or does it feel to you like they're just not seeing something obvious that's actually there?

Like I was just saying, I hear them when they tell me the owners already had a plan. I understand the words they're saying. But... yeah, it feels like they're just blind to what's right in front of them. 

To me, it's just obvious. I know I poisoned the well there. My ideas brought the whole place down, and everybody is suffering now because of me. It really doesn't matter what anyone else tries to tell me, because I just know it's my fault.

If someone you trust showed you concrete evidence—like emails or documents proving the new owners planned these changes months before you ever had any ideas—would that change your mind about being responsible for what happened at the bar, or would you still believe you caused it?

Honestly... I don't think it would matter. Like I was just saying, I know people keep telling me the owners had their plan before any of this even started. Even if someone showed me emails or paperwork... I just can't shake the fact that I poisoned that place somehow. 

It's hard to explain, but... I know my ideas ruined the bar. And now everybody there is paying for it because of me. Seeing documents wouldn't really change anything, because I just know I caused it.

When you say you 'know' you poisoned the bar with your ideas, even though people show you evidence otherwise—do you recognize that this belief doesn't make logical sense, or does it feel completely real and true to you in the moment, the way a fact would?

It feels completely real to me. Like a fact. I know people keep telling me the owners had their plan before any of this, and I hear them, but... it doesn't change how real it is to me. I just can't shake the fact that I poisoned that place somehow. It's not about logic. It's just that I know my ideas ruined the bar, and now everybody there is paying for it because of me. That's just the truth of it to me.

When you asked me earlier if you'd ever had another period lasting at least two weeks where you felt depressed, you said this was the first time it's been this bad. But I want to make sure I understand clearly: have you ever had any period in your life—even if it wasn't as severe as what you're experiencing now—where you felt depressed or down for at least two weeks?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I've had bad days here and there, like anybody else, but... nothing that lasted two weeks. This is the first time I've ever felt anything like this. Before this started, I was always pretty steady.
